craft_evidence.owned: yes, evidenced: "We make our shirts at our workshop in Andover, under the guidance of Di Bainbridge and Gwenda Witts. They joined the company in 1969 and 1976" (/pages/our-workshop); boxer shorts "Made at our Andover workshop"; silk pyjama cloth "washed at our Andover workshop"
craft_evidence.makers: own workshop named (Andover); knitwear says "Made in Scotland" without naming the knitter
craft_evidence.mills: yes: Alumo (Swiss poplin, boxer cloth), Thomas Mason, Loro Piana (cashmere yarn, linen cloth), Solbiati, Fox Brothers (flannel gowns), Holland (herringbone) named on product pages
craft_evidence.madein: 32/102 styles state a making country on the product page (England, Scotland, London)
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: "since its foundation in 1910 ... the heart of Jermyn Street in the Piccadilly Arcade since day one"; founder Harold Budd (/pages/about-us)
craft_evidence.process: partial: finishing-board inspection at Andover, hand-piped nightwear, hand-pleated dress shirts, 2-fold 100s poplin described on product pages
craft_evidence.reasoning: Budd names its own Andover workshop and the two long-serving staff who run it, and product pages name the cloth mills (Alumo, Thomas Mason, Loro Piana). Shirts and nightwear come from that workshop; knitwear and some cloth goods are bought in without a named maker, so it stops at 4.
